headline: Maya reaches the real app gate knowing the three-step workflow, available models, export formats, and credit model she is evaluating.
overview: A live product-level walk for AutoBounds, framed around Maya Thornton's actual decision rather than a list of routes.
targetAudience: Runs mapping operations for a regional agriculture team and needs a faster first pass before GIS review. She cares about accepted boundaries and export compatibility, not an impressive model name on its own.

steps.title: The outcome is stated before the machinery
steps.action: Opened the public AutoBounds product page.
steps.description: The promise is concrete: turn manual delineation into an export-ready starting point from satellite imagery.

steps.title: The workflow is point, process, export
steps.description: Maya can see what she must provide, what the model does, and what leaves the system before she evaluates implementation detail.
steps.screenshotAlt: The three-step AutoBounds field mapping workflow

steps.title: Models are compared by operating trade-offs
steps.description: The model page makes speed, prompting, and boundary quality part of the product decision instead of presenting AI as one opaque button.

steps.title: Credits map to accepted work
steps.description: Pricing explains that one credit buys one extraction and is deducted only when a result is accepted, which is the operational unit Maya needed.
steps.screenshotAlt: AutoBounds credit pricing and acceptance model

steps.title: The real application starts at an account gate
steps.action: Opened the production app demo route.
steps.description: The walkthrough stops honestly at the production sign-in surface; projects, Labs, and exports remain blocked without an authenticated workspace.
